issues.title: Logic inversion in hasPendingInviteByUserId method
issues.description: The hasPendingInviteByUserId method checks for accepted:true memberships instead of accepted:false (pending invites). This inverts the method's logic - it will return true when users have accepted team memberships rather than pending invites. This breaks the onboarding flow for users with team invites, causing users with accepted memberships to be redirected to personal onboarding instead of users with pending invites. The method name and its intended purpose clearly indicate it should check for pending (non-accepted) invites.

issues.title: Incorrect conditional operator in onboarding redirect logic
issues.description: The conditional logic for redirecting users with pending invites uses OR (||) instead of AND (&&). This means users will be redirected to '/onboarding/personal/settings' if they have a pending invite OR if onboarding-v3 is enabled, rather than requiring both conditions. This breaks the normal onboarding flow - any user with onboarding-v3 enabled will be incorrectly redirected to personal settings regardless of whether they have pending invites. The intended behavior was to only redirect users who have both onboarding-v3 enabled AND a pending invite.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #26829 - fix: add server-side redirect for users with pending invites on onboarding page

structured_output.summary:
The PR adds a server-side redirect on `/onboarding/getting-started` for users who have a pending team invite, so they skip the plan-selection page and go to `/onboarding/personal/settings`. It adds `MembershipRepository.hasPendingInviteByUserId`, uses it in the page, and swaps a direct `prisma.membership.findFirst` in `onboardingUtils.ts` for the repository call. It also adds integration tests for the new method.

The intent is reasonable, but the implementation has a blocking bug. The new method queries `accepted: true` while its name and the PR description both say it should find `accepted: false` invites. As written, every user with any accepted team membership is treated as having a pending invite. The same method feeds `checkOnboardingRedirect`, where the condition was also changed from `&&` to `||`, which reroutes every caller (root page and event-types page) whenever the `onboarding-v3` flag is on. The added integration tests assert the intended semantics, so two of the four fail against this code.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The inverted `accepted` filter is a correctness bug that misroutes most team members on the onboarding page. The `&&` → `||` change in `checkOnboardingRedirect` is an unrelated, rollout-wide routing regression. The integration tests contradict the implementation, so the test evidence the PR relies on does not hold. These need fixing before merge.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, new users who arrive through an invite token are routed by `checkOnboardingRedirect` in `packages/features/auth/lib/onboardingUtils.ts`. Callers are the root `apps/web/app/page.tsx` and the event-types page. Its result depends on the user's onboarding state, the email-verification gate, and the `onboarding-v3` flag. The `/onboarding/getting-started` server page (`apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/onboarding/getting-started/page.tsx`) has no routing logic of its own and always renders `OnboardingView`. Client-side code then performs the invite-based redirect.

This PR adds a server-side guard to that page. It calls a new static `MembershipRepository.hasPendingInviteByUserId`, which should return true when a membership has `accepted: false`, and redirects to `/onboarding/personal/settings` if so. The same repository method replaces the inline Prisma query in `onboardingUtils.ts`, and the routing condition there changes from `pendingInvite && onboardingV3Enabled` to `hasPendingInvite || onboardingV3Enabled`. In the current code the repository query uses `accepted: true`, so the boolean means 'has any accepted membership' rather than 'has a pending invite'.
steps: Entry point: a signed-in user requests `/onboarding/getting-started`. The page resolves the session with `getServerSession` and redirects to `/auth/login` if there is no user id (page.tsx lines 22-26).

New guard: the page calls `MembershipRepository.hasPendingInviteByUserId({ userId })` and redirects to `/onboarding/personal/settings` when it returns true (page.tsx lines 28-33). This is the only place the PR changes page behavior.

Repository method: `hasPendingInviteByUserId` is a static Prisma `findFirst` on the membership table with `accepted: true` (MembershipRepository.ts lines 584-596). The filter is the reversed one. It should match `accepted: false` to represent a pending invite.

Shared routing: `checkOnboardingRedirect` now calls the same method (onboardingUtils.ts line 67). The `||` on line 69 means that whenever `onboarding-v3` is enabled, every non-completed user is routed to personal settings. This affects the root page and the event-types page, not only the getting-started page.

Tests: the new integration file lives beside the repository and matches the vitest `*.integration-test.ts` include glob. Its assertions currently encode the intended semantics, so they fail against the `accepted: true` query.

findings.title: Repository method filters `accepted: true`, so it finds accepted members, not pending invites
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/membership/repositories/MembershipRepository.ts`, the `hasPendingInviteByUserId` method (around lines 584-596) filters the membership query with `accepted: true`, but the method name and the PR intent require a pending invite, so the filter should be `accepted: false`. Change that single filter so the method returns true only when the user has at least one unaccepted membership. Keep the rest of the query unchanged. Then re-run the four integration tests in `MembershipRepository.integration-test.ts` to confirm the expectations agree with the implementation.

findings.title: `||` in checkOnboardingRedirect reroutes every user when onboarding-v3 is enabled
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/auth/lib/onboardingUtils.ts`, `checkOnboardingRedirect` (around lines 64-73) was changed from `pendingInvite && onboardingV3Enabled` to `hasPendingInvite || onboardingV3Enabled`. The original `&&` semantics should be restored so only users with a pending invite under the v3 flag are sent to personal settings. Keep the repository-based lookup introduced in this PR, and make sure the final ternary still returns the correct getting-started path for non-invited users. Do not change the callers in `apps/web/app/page.tsx` or the event-types page.

findings.title: Integration tests assert the opposite of what the method returns
findings.body:
The new tests are meant to pin down `hasPendingInviteByUserId`, but two of them contradict the implementation as written:

- The 'pending invite (accepted: false)' test creates an unaccepted membership and expects `true` (line 70). The query selects `accepted: true`, so the result is `false` and this test fails.
- The 'no pending invites (all accepted)' test creates an accepted membership and expects `false` (line 97). The query returns `true`, so this test also fails.
- The 'both accepted and pending' test (line 158) expects `true` when a second team exists. That matches the wrong query only by accident. When there is no second team, it expects `false` while the only membership is accepted, so it also fails.

The PR's checklist says the tests prove the feature works. Against this code they do not, and the suite will be red in CI.

::diff{file="packages/features/membership/repositories/MembershipRepository.integration-test.ts" lines="50-70"}

::callout{type="warning"}
Fixing the query to `accepted: false` makes tests 1 and 2 pass. Test 4 should drop its conditional expectation (`team2 ? true : false`) and instead create the second team explicitly, so the expected value does not depend on which teams already exist in the database.
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/membership/repositories/MembershipRepository.integration-test.ts`, the 'pending invite' test (around line 50-70) expects `true` for an unaccepted membership, and the 'all accepted' test (around lines 77-101) expects `false` for an accepted membership. These match the intended semantics. Once `hasPendingInviteByUserId` in `MembershipRepository.ts` filters on `accepted: false`, they should pass. Also rewrite the 'both accepted and pending' test (around lines 119-161) so it always creates a second team rather than using `team2 ? true : false`, which hides the no-second-team case. Keep the assertions observable, not tied to internal query calls.

findings.title: Page-level redirect skips the onboarding-completed and email-verification gates
findings.body:
`checkOnboardingRedirect` only sends a user to onboarding when `!user.completedOnboarding`, when the user was created after the onboarding cutoff date, and when they are not in an organization. The new guard on the getting-started page checks only for an invite and skips all of those gates.

With the query fixed to `accepted: false`, any user who still has an unaccepted invite row will be redirected to `/onboarding/personal/settings` every time they open the getting-started page, even if they finished onboarding long ago. Invites to teams the user never joined stay in that state indefinitely. The page also does not run the email-verification check that the root page performs first.

::code{file="apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/onboarding/getting-started/page.tsx" lines="28-33"}

This is an edge case the human checklist already flags, and the PR does not address it.
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/onboarding/getting-started/page.tsx`, the new invite guard (around lines 28-33) redirects any user with a membership that matches `hasPendingInviteByUserId`, without checking `completedOnboarding` or the onboarding cutoff date that `checkOnboardingRedirect` in `packages/features/auth/lib/onboardingUtils.ts` applies. Decide whether already-onboarded users with stale unaccepted invites should be excluded, and if so, apply the same gating. Prefer reusing the existing `checkOnboardingRedirect` logic over duplicating those checks in the page.

findings.title: Static repository method bypasses the injected Prisma client
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/membership/repositories/MembershipRepository.ts`, `hasPendingInviteByUserId` (around lines 584-596) is `static` and uses the module-level `prisma` import, while `hasAcceptedMembershipByEmail` nearby uses `this.prismaClient`. Make the method consistent with the class: either convert it to an instance method using `this.prismaClient` and update the two callers (`apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/onboarding/getting-started/page.tsx` and `packages/features/auth/lib/onboardingUtils.ts`), or accept an optional client parameter. Also check that the method name matches the `accepted` filter it applies.

findings.title: Integration tests leak data on failure and write into a shared team
findings.body:
Two problems in the test setup:

- Cleanup happens at the end of each test body, not in `afterEach` or `try/finally`. If an assertion fails, the created users and memberships are left behind. The `afterEach` only clears `createdMembershipIds`, which is cleared in the test body anyway, so a failure leaks the user row.
- `beforeAll` picks an arbitrary existing team (`findFirst where slug not null`) and attaches test memberships to it. In a shared dev or CI database this writes to real team data, and the membership rows still reference that team when the test fails.

Creating a dedicated team in `beforeAll` and tracking every created user in an array cleaned up in `afterAll` would remove both problems.

::code{file="packages/features/membership/repositories/MembershipRepository.integration-test.ts" lines="22-37"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/membership/repositories/MembershipRepository.integration-test.ts`, the `beforeAll` (around lines 22-37) reuses an arbitrary existing team from the database, and each test deletes its own user and memberships only at the end of its body. Create a dedicated test team in `beforeAll` and delete it in `afterAll`. Track every created user id in an array and delete them in `afterEach` so a failed assertion does not leak rows. Follow the cleanup style of the existing `clearTestMemberships` helper.

findings.title: Unrelated formatting churn and a single-quoted string in a changed file
findings.body:
Several edits in this PR are formatting only and make the diff harder to review:

- The imports in `getting-started/page.tsx` were reordered and a blank separator removed.
- The ternary in `onboardingUtils.ts` was reflowed without a logic change.
- The import specifiers in `MembershipRepository.ts` and the `hasAcceptedMembershipByEmail` signature were reflowed.

Also, the new line `const userEmail = session.user.email || '';` uses single quotes, while the rest of the file and the repo's formatter use double quotes.

::diff{file="apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/onboarding/getting-started/page.tsx" lines="35-35"}

It would be cleaner to revert the unrelated reflows and keep the functional change focused.
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/onboarding/getting-started/page.tsx`, line 35 uses single quotes in `session.user.email || ''`. Change it to double quotes to match the rest of the file and the formatter. Revert the unrelated import reordering at the top of the file, the blank-line removal, and the reflowed ternary in `packages/features/auth/lib/onboardingUtils.ts` and the reflowed signature in `packages/features/membership/repositories/MembershipRepository.ts`, so the diff only contains the functional change.

findings.title: Good: keeping the invite check in the repository removes direct Prisma from onboardingUtils
findings.body: Moving the membership lookup out of `onboardingUtils.ts` into `MembershipRepository` is the right direction and follows the repo's rule against Prisma calls outside repositories. Sharing one helper between the getting-started page and `checkOnboardingRedirect` also means both paths use the same definition of 'has invite'. Once the query and the routing condition are corrected, this will be easier to reason about than the previous inline query.
